newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 40 AHEAD WORLD CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 40 AHEAD WORLD CUP TIE.

text.p: Belgian police said on Saturday afternoon they had detained around 40 football supporters ahead of the evening World Cup clash between Belgium and the Netherland.

"We have made many arrests of both Belgian and Dutch supporters," police spokesman Michael Jonniaux said. "Most of them are arrests for drunkeness or showing aggressive behaviour towards shoppers and tourists."
Belga news agency reported that motorway police had also stopped five Dutch supporters heading to Brussels carrying weapons but with no identification or tickets for the match.
Jonniaux said one or two fights had broken out but so far there been no serious clashes between rival groups of supporters. Charges were likely to be brought in only one or two cases.
Belgian police are taking no chances with the match, deploying more than 1,500 officers, 150 mounted policemen, water cannon and 20 dog teams to patrol Brussels' metro system.

The match was being played at the Heysel stadium where 39 fans were crushed to death by a wall which collapsed when Juventas and Liverpool supporters clashed at the European Cup final in 1985. The stadium has since been rebuilt and renamed after former Belgian monarch King Baudouin.
